basis: Thresholds are a shipped reference baseline, the same for every installation: the per-session p90 of a 90-session spike on one reference machine (Claude Code 2.1.275-2.1.287, 2026-10-02), approved by the maintainer at plan Phase 6 entry, unless a rule's basis names another source; a session above a threshold is an outlier against that baseline, not wrong in absolute terms. Every number in a rule's basis comes from those reference measurements, not from the store being swept. A null threshold reports the metric without a finding.
recheck: a Claude Code release changes a canary-fed metric, or a swept store's own p90 for a thresholded metric exceeds stale_p90_factor times its threshold. The trigger is one-sided: a p90 below the threshold never fires it, and a threshold of 0 fires on any p90 above 0. sweep.py marks such a metric baseline_stale

rules.basis: main-session output tokens per session; spike median 72738, p90 205212
subagent output tokens per session; spike median 7467, p90 72347
input tokens re-sent after a reported cache miss per session; spike median 0, p90 272137, 18 of 90 sessions nonzero
share of cache-write tokens at the 5-minute TTL, machine-wide; spike 0.84 (subagents about 1.0, main about 0); no per-session spread to set a threshold from

active seconds per session, read from the main session's record timestamps (store field time.active_gap_s): the sum of gaps between consecutive user, assistant and system records, each capped at the 300 s idle boundary (a judgment value, the same as idle_gaps_gt5m), so it never exceeds wall clock. It approximates Claude Code's native claude_code.active_time.total metric from transcript timestamps and is a second definition beside it. Internal-format read: the earlier definition summed turn_duration records, which are sparse and can time a turn begun in a previous transcript (76 of 764 sessions above wall clock, Claude Code 2.1.241-2.1.288, audit 2026-10-03); time.active_s no longer reads them. Threshold null until #6077 re-derives it on this definition (the old 26064 s came from turn_duration sums)
/clear commands per session; spike p90 1, max 1, 33 of 90 sessions start with /clear as the handoff routine, so a threshold would flag normal use
typed human turns per session; spike median 3, p90 14

main-session interrupts per session; spike median 0, p90 0, max 2, 3 of 90 sessions nonzero. Raised from 0 to 1 by operator decision (#6076): the first full store (2026-10-03, 764 sessions) had p90 1, and 57 of the 81 sessions threshold 0 flagged had exactly one interrupt; threshold 1 flags 24
tool denials per session; spike median 3, p90 27
subagents spawned per session; spike median 6, p90 33

a session's p90 Stop wait, read from stop_hook_summary records (store field stop_hooks.wait_ms_p90): per Stop run the slowest hookInfos[].durationMs, since matching hooks run in parallel and the person waits for the slowest. Internal-format read: that durationMs is each hook's own run time is inferred, not documented (Claude Code 2.1.241-2.1.288; across 7,843 multi-hook Stop records the observed wait was at least the max in every record, audit 2026-10-03). The earlier definition summed the hooks (stop_hooks.ms_p90, still stored). Threshold null until #6077 re-derives it on this definition. Route kept by owner decision (2026-10-11): /harness-ops:audit-performance is the skill that tunes hook cost, even though its engine does not read transcripts; recheck when #6033 (whether harness-ops summarizes recorded hook durations) is decided

edits to one path within one linked PR, summed over the sessions that link only that PR; second spike (320 interactive sessions, Claude Code 2.1.280-2.1.296, 2026-10-13): 46 single-PR sessions, 43 PRs, 1581 path-PR pairs, median 1, p90 5, p99 19
